title: Bounded flat module complexes have Tor amplitude in their support interval
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and choose its derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with the ordinary K-flat derived tensor product. Let $P^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $R$-modules, and let $a,b\in\mathbf Z$. Suppose $P^i=0$ whenever $i<a$ or $b<i$, and every $P^i$ is flat, meaning that tensoring with it preserves exact sequences of modules. Then $Q(P)$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$: for every $R$-module $M$ in degree zero, $H^i(Q(P)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M[0])=0$ whenever $i<a$ or $b<i$. No ordering of $a,b$, finite generation, locality, or Noetherian hypothesis is required.

proof.text: The bounded-above flat complex P is K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat], in the sense of [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. The existing source theorem uses its proved bounded variant CochainComplex.kFlat_of_bounded_of_flat. For modules, categorical flatness and module flatness agree by ModuleCat.flat_iff_flat.

For each ordinary module M, use [lem-weil-pbc-source-kflat-tensor-single-model] to identify Q(P) tensor-derived M[0] with Q of the complex P tensor M. That complex has the same zero terms outside [a,b]; its cohomology vanishes there. This is precisely the existing proved generic theorem DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn_Q_obj_of_flat specialized to ModuleCat R. For a greater than b the complex is zero, so the conclusion still holds.
